html.body: REM1499455565,6125432016-12-212016-12-21REM DOCUMENTApplication No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000REMARKSApplicant submits this Reply in response to the Office Action mailed on September 23, 2016.Status of the ClaimsClaims 1-20 are currently pending in this application. By this Amendment, Applicant amends claims 1, 3-7, 9, 11-15, 17, 19, and 20. The originally filed specification and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended claims, for example, at paragraph [035]. Applicant believes that this Amendment adds no new matter.Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the pending rejections for at least the reasons that follow.Section 112 RejectionsClaims 1-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) (pre-AIA) (first paragraph) as allegedly failing to comply with the enablement requirement for reciting, "determining blood flow demand based on a received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel." To expedite prosecution, claims 3, 11, and 19 have been amended to recite, "determining the blood flow characteristic based on the received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel." Support for the amendment is provided, for example, at paragraph [0029] of the original specification, which states, "[f]or example, a patient's tissue may have higher blood flow demand during an exercise state, than during a patient's resting state. Accounting for physiological state in determining a blood flow characteristic may provide greater context or accuracy in the resultant determined blood flow characteristic."-12-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000Claims 1-20 were also rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) (pre-AIA) (firstparagraph) as allegedly failing to comply with the enablement requirement. With the amendments of this Reply, the allegedly noncompliant recitation now reads as follows: "generating or displaying an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to a tissue region of the patient's viscera or bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic, or generating or displaying a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic and an expected blood flow characteristic associated with a tissue region of the patient's bowel." The Office Action rejects the claim feature on the basis that "the scope of the claimed invention encompasses an extremely large number of possibilities." (Office Action, pages 6 and 7.)Section 2164.08 of the MPEP states, "[w]ith respect to the breadth of a claim, therelevant concern is whether the scope of enablement provided to one skilled in the art by the disclosure is commensurate with the scope of protection sought by the claims. AK Steel Corp. v. Sollac, 344 F.3d 1234, 1244, 68 USPQ2d 1280, 1287 (Fed. Cir. 2003); In reMoore, 439 F.2d 1232, 1236, 169 USPQ 236, 239 (CCPA 1971). See also Plant Genetic Sys., N. V. v. DeKalb Genetics Corp., 315 F.3d 1335, 1339, 65 USPQ2d 1452, 1455 (Fed. Cir. 2003) (alleged "pioneer status" of invention irrelevant to enablement determination)." For this case, exemplary FIGs. 3 and 4 and their corresponding descriptions in the original specification provide enablement to one skilled in the art that is commensurate with the scope of protection sought by the claims. For example, paragraph [048] of the original specification states, "step 309 may include comparing the patient blood flow characteristic against the predetermined threshold or-13-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000average blood flow characteristic (e.g., from step 305). Based on the comparison, step 309 may include a making a determination of blood supply adequacy." As another example, paragraph [049] of the original specification states, "[v]arious conditions may be triggered by various levels of blood supply inadequacy. Step 311 may include determining patient risk for one or more conditions, e.g., based on blood supply adequacy at one or more locations in the modeled bowel." The scope of enablement provided to one skilled in the art by paragraphs [048] and [049] of the original disclosure is commensurate with the scope of protection sought by the claims.The Office Action also states, "the determination of blood flow demand being inferred from a patient's liver mass is non-enabled and would require undue experimentation to determine." (Office Action, page 4.) However, the currently- amended independent claims recite, "determining a mass of the portion of the patient's bowel; determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel based on the determined mass." (Emphasis added.) The claims do not recite determining blood flow demand from a patient's liver mass.Claim 3 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) (pre-AIA) (second paragraph) as allegedly being indefinite. The current amendment renders the rejection moot.Applicant thus requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the Section 112 rejections.Section 103 RejectionsApplicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claims 1-20, which were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Taylor (U.S. Publication No. 2012/0041318 A1) ("Taylor") in view of T. Mabotuwana, L. Cheng, and A. Pullan,-14-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000("A model of blood flow in the mesenteric arterial system" Biomed Eng Online. 2007) ("Mabotuwana").To expedite prosecution, Applicant amends the claims to recite, "determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel based on the determined mass; [and] determining, using the blood flow demand, a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel." Neither Taylor nor Mabotuwana, individually or in combination, would have rendered obvious the above-recited subject matter.For the reasons discussed, Applicant submits that claims 1-20 are allowable over all of the cited references. Accordingly, Applicant requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the Section 103 rejections.Double Patenting RejectionsIn the Office Action, claims 1-20 were provisionally rejected based onnonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 21-40 of copending divisional U.S. Application No. 15/080,829. Without conceding to the assertions in the double patenting rejections, Applicant requests that the Examiner hold the double patenting rejections in abeyance until such time as no other issues remain in the application, and the pending claims are deemed otherwise allowable. At that time, Applicant will investigate the need for any terminal disclaimers.ConclusionThe Office Action contains characterization of the claims and the related art with which the applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.-15-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to beunderstood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.If the Examiner believes a telephone conversation might advance prosecution, the Examiner is invited to call applicant's undersigned representative at 202-803-8075.Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account No. 50-5906. In addition, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees due and any other fees due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 or § 1.17 during the pendency of this application to Deposit Account No. 50-5906.Respectfully submitted,BOOKOFF McANDREWS, PLLCCustomer Number: 108,449Dated: December 21, 2016 SVG14994555.12-21-2016.IWZBO3U2RXEAPX1.REM.5.22.1204.2631.2209.2679.svg0.163.35Chemistry Lian HuangReg.
